```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6,
                      fig.height = 4)
has_bench <- requireNamespace("bench", quietly = TRUE)
```

```{r setup}
library(coxlite)
library(survival)
```

This checks that **coxlite** gets the same answers as `survival::coxph()`
and compares the speed of:

* `coxlite` with the C++ engine (`engine = "cpp"`, the default)
* `coxlite` with the pure-R engine (`engine = "R"`)
* `survival::coxph()`, whose core is written in C

## Correctness

### One model in detail

```{r}
f <- Surv(time, status) ~ trt + age + biomarker + sex
fit <- cox_ph(f, data = sim_trial)
ref <- coxph(f, data = sim_trial)

all.equal(coef(fit), coef(ref))
all.equal(vcov(fit), vcov(ref), check.attributes = FALSE)
all.equal(fit$loglik, ref$loglik)
all.equal(fit$score, ref$score)                   # score (log-rank) test
all.equal(fit$wald.test, unname(ref$wald.test))   # Wald test
all.equal(predict(fit), predict(ref, reference = "sample"),
          check.attributes = FALSE)
all.equal(cox_basehaz(fit), basehaz(ref), check.attributes = FALSE)
```

All `TRUE`. The biggest coefficient difference is about
`r signif(max(abs(coef(fit) - coef(ref))), 1)`, so basically rounding error.

### A few more data sets

`compare_fits()` fits a model with both coxlite engines and `coxph()` and
checks if they match.

```{r}
compare_fits <- function(formula, data, ties) {
  a <- cox_ph(formula, data, ties = ties)
  b <- cox_ph(formula, data, ties = ties, engine = "R")
  r <- coxph(formula, data, ties = ties)
  same <- function(x, y) isTRUE(all.equal(x, y, check.attributes = FALSE))
  data.frame(
    ties = ties,
    coef = same(coef(a), coef(r)),
    vcov = same(vcov(a), vcov(r)),
    loglik = same(a$loglik, r$loglik),
    R_vs_cpp = same(coef(a), coef(b)),
    max_abs_diff = format(max(abs(coef(a) - coef(r))), digits = 2)
  )
}
```

Two real data sets from **survival**, and some simulated ones with lots of
ties, strata or more covariates:

```{r}
lung <- survival::lung
lung$status <- lung$status - 1
veteran <- survival::veteran

set.seed(625)
sim_ties <- sim_cox(1000, beta = c(0.5, -0.5, 0.25), round_to = 2)
sim_strat <- sim_cox(2000, beta = c(0.5, 0, -0.3, 1), n_strata = 5,
                     round_to = 0.5, shape = 2)
sim_wide <- sim_cox(3000, beta = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 10), round_to = 1)

scenarios <- list(
  "sim_trial + strata" = list(Surv(time, status) ~ trt + age + biomarker +
                                strata(center), sim_trial),
  "lung (factor)"      = list(Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex +
                                factor(ph.ecog), lung),
  "veteran + strata"   = list(Surv(time, status) ~ karno + age + trt +
                                strata(celltype), veteran),
  "sim heavy ties"     = list(Surv(time, status) ~ x1 + x2 + x3, sim_ties),
  "sim 5 strata"       = list(Surv(time, status) ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 +
                                strata(stratum), sim_strat),
  "sim p = 10"         = list(Surv(time, status) ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 +
                                x6 + x7 + x8 + x9 + x10, sim_wide)
)

results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(scenarios), function(nm) {
  s <- scenarios[[nm]]
  rbind(cbind(scenario = nm, compare_fits(s[[1]], s[[2]], "efron")),
        cbind(scenario = nm, compare_fits(s[[1]], s[[2]], "breslow")))
}))
knitr::kable(results)
```

All `r nrow(results)` fits match.

## Efficiency

Timing with `bench::mark()` (which also checks the three give the same
coefficients):

```{r, eval = has_bench}
fit_coefs <- function(data, ...) {
  unname(coef(cox_ph(Surv(time, status) ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5, data, ...)))
}
ref_coefs <- function(data) {
  unname(coef(coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5, data)))
}

set.seed(1)
d <- sim_cox(5000, beta = c(0.5, -0.5, 0.25, 1, 0), round_to = 0.5)
bm <- bench::mark(
  coxlite_cpp = fit_coefs(d),
  coxlite_R   = fit_coefs(d, engine = "R"),
  survival    = ref_coefs(d),
  iterations = 20, filter_gc = FALSE
)
bm[, c("expression", "min", "median", "itr/sec", "mem_alloc")]
```

### Scaling with sample size

```{r scaling, eval = has_bench, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
sizes <- c(1000, 5000, 20000)
timings <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sizes, function(n) {
  set.seed(n)
  d <- sim_cox(n, beta = c(0.5, -0.5, 0.25, 1, 0), round_to = 0.5)
  b <- bench::mark(
    coxlite_cpp = fit_coefs(d),
    coxlite_R   = fit_coefs(d, engine = "R"),
    survival    = ref_coefs(d),
    min_iterations = 3, max_iterations = 10, filter_gc = FALSE
  )
  data.frame(n = n, method = as.character(b$expression),
             median_ms = as.numeric(b$median) * 1000)
}))
wide <- reshape(timings, idvar = "n", timevar = "method", direction = "wide")
names(wide) <- sub("median_ms.", "", names(wide), fixed = TRUE)
rownames(wide) <- NULL
wide$cpp_speedup_over_R <- wide$coxlite_R / wide$coxlite_cpp
knitr::kable(wide, digits = 1, caption = "Median time (ms)")
```

```{r scaling-plot, eval = has_bench}
cols <- c(coxlite_cpp = "#1b9e77", coxlite_R = "#d95f02", survival = "#7570b3")
plot(NULL, xlim = range(sizes), ylim = range(timings$median_ms), log = "xy",
     xlab = "Sample size n", ylab = "Median time (ms, log scale)")
for (m in names(cols)) {
  s <- timings[timings$method == m, ]
  lines(s$n, s$median_ms, type = "b", pch = 19, col = cols[m])
}
legend("topleft", names(cols), col = cols, lty = 1, pch = 19, bty = "n")
```

## Summary

coxlite matches `coxph()` on everything I checked, for both tie methods and
with or without strata. The C++ engine is about as fast as `coxph()` (it
depends on the machine, and `coxph()` also computes some extra stuff like
residuals). The R engine is a lot slower, mostly because it builds an
n × p² matrix of outer products where the C++ code just keeps running p × p
sums.
